prompt.context: All-Mart, a discount superstore similar to Walmart, is interested in entering the market in Romania and has hired McKinsey to help them determine if it will be profitable. All-Mart is planning on opening their first store in Bucharest, the capital city of Romania.
prompt.question: What factors would you consider to determine if this is a good idea or not?

clarifying_info.q: What is the population of Bucharest?
clarifying_info.a: The population of Bucharest is 2 million people.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average salary or income per person?
clarifying_info.a: The average salary is 1,350 RON per person per month. (3 RON = 1 USD)

clarifying_info.q: How do Romanians spend their money / what are their spending habits?
clarifying_info.a: 30% on food, 40% on rent and utilities, 5% on clothing, 25% on various other items.

clarifying_info.q: What do people spend on electronics?
clarifying_info.a: From an independent study, people in Bucharest spend an average of USD 500 per year on electronics.
There are 5 superstores in the outskirts of Bucharest that collectively cover 30% of the market. The rest of the market is served by smaller stores spread throughout the city.

exhibits.title: Math Part 1 – Market Size Data
exhibits.shows: A table of input data for computing total market size in Bucharest, including population, average salary, spending breakdown by category, electronics spend, and currency conversion rate

exhibits.title: Math Part 2 – Cost Structure Overview
exhibits.shows: A reference to a cost comparison handout showing cost categories as a percent of U.S. costs for Romania, with additional context on supply sources

exhibits.title: Handout – Cost by Category: U.S. vs. Romania
exhibits.shows: A table comparing percentage of total cost by category (Food, Clothing, Electronics, Salaries) between the U.S. and Romania (Romania column is blank for candidate to fill in), plus additional information about supply sources for each category

additional_info: Food is supplied from local distributors
Clothing is produced by contractors in Asia – same as in the U.S.
Electronics are supplied by branded organizations (Sony, HP, etc.) – same as in the U.S.
Romanian salary is 5 times less than salary in the U.S.

framework: Market Conditions (Revenue): Assess market size and growth potential; understand purchasing behaviors and customer segmentation in Romania
Costs: Estimate costs of opening and operating a store in Bucharest – COGS (direct labor, direct materials, shipping/logistics, overhead) and SG&A; consider opportunity cost
Strategy: Evaluate fit with All-Mart's overall strategy and culture; assess prior experience in global market entry; consider first-mover advantage and competitive response

questions.prompt: Compute the total addressable market size for All-Mart in Bucharest.
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies the two main spending categories relevant to a superstore (food/clothing and electronics), applies the spending percentages to income, annualizes, and converts to USD. The candidate should then estimate a realistic market share given the competitive landscape (5 superstores split 30% evenly = ~6% each; assume All-Mart captures roughly one superstore share of ~10%) and derive a dollar figure for All-Mart's realistic revenue opportunity.

math.setup: Total Market = Food/Clothing spend + Electronics spend across Bucharest's 2M population
steps: Realistic All-Mart share: 5 superstores cover 30% evenly → each has ~6%; assume ~10% share for All-Mart (one superstore equivalent)
All-Mart market size = 4,780,000,000 × 10% ≈ 478,000,000 USD; casebook rounds to ~239M USD (using 50% of 10% share or a ~5% capture rate)
math.answer: Total market ~4.78B USD/year; All-Mart's realistic capture ~239M USD/year

questions.prompt: Now assess the cost side. What is the overall cost of running a discount store in Romania as a percent of U.S. costs? Which categories have savings and why?
questions.guidance: A strong answer recognizes that costs tied to local resources (food sourcing, local salaries) will be significantly cheaper in Romania, while costs for globally sourced goods (clothing from Asia, branded electronics) remain the same as in the U.S. The candidate should work through each cost category using the exhibit's U.S. percentage weights, apply the Romania cost factor, and sum to get total Romania costs as a percent of U.S. costs.

math.setup: Each cost category's Romania cost = U.S. weight × Romania cost factor. Food: local supply → much cheaper; Clothing: Asia contractors same → same cost; Electronics: global brands same → same cost; Salaries: 5× lower in Romania.
steps: Food (20% of U.S. total cost): local distributors → cost ≈ 1/5 of U.S. → Romania food cost = 20% × (1/5) = 4% of U.S. total
Clothing (20% of U.S. total cost): same Asia contractors → same cost → 20% of U.S. total
Electronics (40% of U.S. total cost): same global brands → same cost → 40% of U.S. total
Salaries (20% of U.S. total cost): 5× lower → Romania salary cost = 20% × (1/5) = 4% of U.S. total
Total Romania cost = 4% + 20% + 40% + 4% = 68% of U.S. total cost
math.answer: Running the store in Romania costs approximately 68% of what it would cost in the U.S., primarily due to savings in food sourcing and local labor.

brainstorming.prompt: What other factors should All-Mart consider when determining a realistic market share capture in Romania?

categories.name: Competitive Dynamics
ideas: Current superstore incumbents may respond aggressively with price cuts or promotions
Smaller local stores may have loyal customer relationships and location advantages
Potential for new entrants if Romania market proves attractive

categories.name: Consumer Behavior
ideas: Romanian shopping habits may favor local markets and smaller neighborhood stores
Brand familiarity with All-Mart may be low; marketing investment needed
Price sensitivity vs. quality expectations of emerging-market consumers

categories.name: Regulatory & Political
ideas: Foreign ownership regulations or restrictions on retail
Zoning and permitting requirements for large-format stores
Import tariffs or customs costs on non-locally sourced goods

categories.name: Operational & Logistics
ideas: Supply chain reliability for perishable goods from local distributors
Infrastructure quality (roads, logistics networks) impacting cost assumptions
Availability of skilled local management and workforce

categories.name: Strategic Fit
ideas: All-Mart's prior experience (or lack thereof) in emerging market entry
First-mover advantage if competition is currently limited
Whether Romania entry fits a broader Eastern European expansion strategy

recommendation: The Romanian market presents a meaningful opportunity: the Bucharest addressable market is ~4.78B USD/year, and with a realistic ~5–10% share All-Mart could capture ~240–480M USD in annual revenue

Cost structure is favorable — operating costs in Romania are approximately 68% of U.S. costs, driven by cheaper local food sourcing and significantly lower salaries, providing a structural margin advantage
All-Mart should proceed with entering Bucharest, but conduct further due diligence on competitive response, consumer adoption, and regulatory requirements before committing capital
risks: Incumbent superstores may respond aggressively, limiting All-Mart's ability to capture assumed market share
Consumer loyalty to local stores and unfamiliarity with the All-Mart brand could slow adoption
Regulatory hurdles or infrastructure limitations could increase actual costs above the 68% estimate
Currency and macroeconomic risk in an emerging market (RON/USD fluctuation)
next_steps: Conduct consumer research to validate willingness to shop at a large-format discount superstore
Assess specific site options and zoning/permitting requirements in Bucharest
Model full P&L including build-out capex, ramp-up timeline, and break-even analysis
Evaluate competitive response scenarios and develop a market entry pricing strategy
